newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT, Dutch PTT settle names row.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT, Dutch PTT settle names row.

text.p: Dutch paper group KNP BT and post and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN) said on Tuesday they had settled a dispute over the abbreviated form of their names.

In a joint statement they said KNP BT would change its name in the course of 1998 and that PTT Nederland would contribute to the costs involved, including an advertising campaign to publicise the new name which has yet to be chosen.
KNP BT had started legal action against PTT Nederland, arguing that the latter's abbreviated name KPN could be confused with that of KNP BT. This action will now be dropped.
"We are very satisfied with the decision...this is the best solution," KNP BT's spokesman Patrick de Leede said.

Van Leede declined to put a figure on the sum of money involved in the settlement, but said it was debatable whether PTT Nederland had emerged victorious from the dispute in view of the amount agreed.
The name change will not affect KNP BT's paper unit KNP Leykam, the two companies added.
